LEARNING PATH · CLASS 43 · OUR EARTH & SPACE · AGES 4–5

Our Earth & Space — twenty-four printable space flashcards to download and print.

Twenty-four printable Earth and space flashcards for ages four to five, all on this one page, in six shelves: my blue planet, the sun’s family, the spinning day, weather and world, rockets and astronauts, and the stars to finish. Every card carries its idea in words YOU can say back — the sun lights our day; Earth spins once and that makes tomorrow; gravity keeps your feet on the ground — with Download and Print buttons right under the picture. Pick a card, print it, and the universe walks into your kitchen: planets at breakfast, weather words on the walk, a countdown to blastoff before bath.

Back to the Learning Path ↗
HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

One sky idea. The child says it. Then the sky does the teaching.

Every card prints one Earth-and-space idea the way a four-year-old meets it: what the sun is doing, why the moon changes shape, where the rain comes from, how a rocket gets off the ground. The small words under each picture are the idea itself, said kid-first — day is when our side of Earth faces the sun; a comet drags its tail; look up and count the stars you can see. The Download button saves the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer. Space words grow the same way the cards run — big ideas, small words, said again and again.

The shelves follow a look-up day. My Blue Planet starts with the ground, the water and the air — the parts of Earth you can touch today. The Sun’s Family lines up the planets, from our own sun and moon out to Neptune. The Spinning Day shelf answers the bedtime question — why does the sun come up? Weather & World reads the sky outside the window and lays out the whole map, equator to poles. Rockets & Astronauts counts down to blastoff with the gear real space travelers use. And the Stars shelf finishes far, far away — comets, constellations, galaxies and one friendly black hole.

Printable Earth flashcards for kids: landforms, rivers and forests, rocks and fossils, and taking care of the water and air — the planet science that starts in your own backyard. AROUND THE SCHOOL

Where the sky learning grows.

Science experiments in Class 31 · Ages 4–5 ↗Weather lessons in Class 34 · Ages 4–5 ↗Day & night cards in Class 41 · Ages 4–5 ↗Science at a Glance sheets · Ages 2–5 ↗The Learning Path ↗

Class 31 runs the experiments — sink or float, magnets, the water cycle — and this class names the planets and the weather those experiments play with. Class 34 walks through every kind of weather day and the clothes that match it, and Class 41 prints the day-and-night routine cards that pair with the spinning Earth right here. Science at a Glance keeps the whole science wall on one page for the youngest scientists. And when the day needs a plan, the Learning Path holds all forty-three classes in order.

Space is not far away — it starts at your window. Every card here hands the sky words to you — the planets, the weather, the countdown — and your grown-up’s whole job is to look up with you.
